_schema.note: Curated to deadlines that materially affect federal-health-IT procurement. Each entry links to an authoritative source plus MMT's read on capture impact. Re-verified 2026-09-25 against the enacted FY2027 continuing resolution; the prior version still described FY2027 appropriations as underway and treated 2026-09-30 as shutdown risk, which the 2026-09-02 CR had already resolved.

deadlines.label: FY26 fiscal year end
deadlines.headline: FY26 appropriations lapse, and the CR is already law, so there is no October 1 shutdown
deadlines.fy_impact: All twelve FY2026 bills were enacted in the Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 and expire tonight. FY2027 opens the next morning under a continuing resolution signed 2026-09-02, so there is no funding gap at the turn of the fiscal year.
deadlines.capture_read: The usual end-of-year obligation push still applies: anything the agency meant to award off FY26 money lands by tonight. What is different from most years is that October 1 carries no shutdown drama, so a slipped award is a program decision, not a funding excuse. If a contracting officer told you the delay was about appropriations, that answer expires with the fiscal year.

deadlines.label: FY27 begins under a continuing resolution
deadlines.headline: New starts are barred until the CR lifts
deadlines.fy_impact: P.L. 119-103 funds all twelve bills at FY2026 rates from 2026-10-01 through 2026-12-11. Section 104 bars new starts. The Defense provisions separately bar DoD from beginning new programs, entering multiyear contracts, or increasing production rates without an exception.
deadlines.capture_read: This is the line that decides your Q1. A new program start needs an enacted appropriation, so anything that was going to begin life in October now waits on December at the earliest. Task orders against an IDIQ you already hold are the safe ground, because the authority sits at the vehicle and does not need new money. If your FY27 pipeline leans on new starts, build the December scenario now and have a task-order list ready to pull forward. For DHA specifically, the multiyear and production-rate bars mean a program hoping to scale this fall will hold at current rate instead.
related_expirations: Section 104 new-start prohibition applies government wide
DoD barred from new programs, multiyear contracts and production-rate increases absent an exception
Division B extends the VA and DoD health care resource sharing incentive program
Division B extends VA authority to collect for nursing home care

deadlines.label: Continuing resolution expires
deadlines.headline: The real FY27 cliff, 38 days after the midterms
deadlines.fy_impact: The CR runs out. Congress passes full-year bills, another CR, or the government shuts down. No FY2027 regular appropriations bill has been enacted, and the Senate Appropriations Committee had not reported any as of the CR's enactment.
deadlines.capture_read: Put this date on every FY27 capture plan. The midterms land first, so whoever controls each chamber in December sets the leverage, and a change in either one raises the odds of a long fight. The FY26 year opened with a 42-day shutdown, so the precedent for a bad December is recent and real. Plan for the new-start freeze to run into January and price the risk into anything whose start date you are promising a customer.

deadlines.label: Calendar year end
deadlines.headline: Health program funding cliffs land twenty days after the CR expires
deadlines.fy_impact: The Community Health Center Fund expires, and it carries roughly seventy percent of federal health center grant funding. National Health Service Corps funding, Medicare clinical laboratory payment relief, and the temporary 2.5 percent Medicare physician payment increase expire the same day.
deadlines.capture_read: Two cliffs inside three weeks is the thing to watch. If the December appropriations fight runs long, these extenders are the hostages, and HRSA grantees and Medicare-billing health systems feel it first. If you sell into community health centers or to physician-practice IT, expect buying decisions to stall through Q1 2027. The health center funding cliff is the one most people miss, because it does not look like an IT deadline until a grantee freezes a project.
related_expirations: Temporary 2.5 percent Medicare physician payment increase

appropriations_status.fy26_status: Enacted. All twelve bills, Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026 (H.R. 7148), signed 2026-02-03. Expires 2026-09-30. FY2026 opened with a 42-day shutdown from 2025-10-01 to 2025-11-11.
appropriations_status.fy27_status: No regular appropriations bill enacted. Funded by continuing resolution: H.R. 6500, the Continuing Appropriations and Extensions Act, 2027 (P.L. 119-103), signed 2026-09-02, covering all twelve bills from 2026-10-01 through 2026-12-11 at FY2026 rates, with a government-wide new-start prohibition.
appropriations_status.cr_history_note: Verified 2026-09-25. The CR is a clean 72-day extension with anomalies, not a full-year measure for any bill, so the December 11 date is a real cliff rather than a formality. An earlier House CR (H.R. 9770, passed 2026-07-21, proposing a December 4 end date) never became law; cite P.L. 119-103 and December 11, not that bill or that date.

fy27_bills._note: Status of the three FY2027 bills that fund MMT's coverage agencies, as of 2026-09-25. None is enacted. Stage matters: committee approval is not House passage, and House passage is not law.

labor_hhs_education.stage: Approved by the House Appropriations Committee, 34 to 28. No House floor vote found. Not enacted.
labor_hhs_education.discretionary_allocation: $189.3 billion, about 3 percent below the FY2026 enacted level

milcon_va.stage: Passed the House 400 to 15 on 2026-05-21. No Senate action found. Not enacted.
milcon_va.discretionary_allocation: $157 billion, nearly $4 billion above the FY2026 enacted level

defense.stage: Reported by the House Appropriations Committee 2026-06-26, approved 34 to 27, and scheduled for floor consideration the week of 2026-06-29. House floor passage is not confirmed, so MMT carries this as committee-reported only. Not enacted.
pending: House floor vote status not confirmed in the 2026-09-25 verification pass
